headline: Deep learning links DNA sequence and chromatin profiles to regulatory variant effects
label: Regulatory Genomics Deep Learning
summary: Sequence and foundation models now predict base-pair regulatory outputs and transfer across cell types, shifting toward context-aware, gene-level outputs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning that maps DNA sequence, chromatin profiles, and expression data onto regulatory and variant-level outcomes. AlphaGenome takes a 1 Mb DNA input and predicts thousands of functional genomic tracks at base-pair resolution. A parameter-efficient fine-tuning study transfers the Borzoi regulatory sequence model to new cell types and assays, cutting runtime. ChromBERT, pre-trained on ChIP-seq data from about 1,000 transcription regulators, learns interpretable context-specific regulatory networks. DeepCE applies bidirectional GRUs and CNNs to gene regulatory network inference from scRNA-seq, while a hierarchical cross-entropy loss improves out-of-distribution scRNA-seq cell type annotation. Volaria integrates coding and regulatory variants into gene-centered representations. What is new is the breadth of inputs and the shift toward context-aware, gene-level outputs. The summaries are abbreviated, so validation and performance claims remain unassessed.
